prop-31c8040db4a92a581c00.normalized_semantic_payload: **Answer-worthiness.** Dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), momentariness (*kṣaṇikavāda*) and no permanent self (*nairātmyavāda*) are the **printed core**. Both senses of the Middle Path (*madhyamā pratipad*; Pali: *majjhimā paṭipadā*), the Four Noble Truths, the twelve links, the five aggregates, cessation of conditioned suffering (*nirvāṇa*), the Three Jewels (*Triratna*) and the four philosophical schools are **marks-essential core**, because no routed previous-year question can be answered without them. The Buddhist theory of the means of valid knowledge (*pramāṇa*), the exclusion theory of meaning (*apoha*), the undeclared questions (*avyākṛta*) and the creator-God critique are **core supporting depth** wherever they decide a routed question. Detailed scholastic taxonomies and the internal Prāsaṅgika–Svātantrika dispute are **optional enrichment** and are held back to the clearly labelled optional block.

prop-f2b8bc427cd1ac3e8833.normalized_semantic_payload: > **Claim.** The Buddha's silence and the Buddhist rejection of a creator are two applications of one methodological principle: refuse explanatory demands that the analysis has already dissolved. > **Named evidence.** The undeclared questions cover the eternity and finitude of the world, the identity of life-principle and body, and the post-mortem status of the Tathāgata; the arrow parable states that they are not conducive to the goal; the fire-going-out simile shows that directional predication lapses once conditions cease; and dependent origination is said to explain arising without a creator. > **Analysis.** Because all four available answers to an undeclared question presuppose a substantial subject of predication, the silence is a rejection of the question's grammar rather than an admission of ignorance; the same logic disqualifies a creator, since a cause invoked outside the conditional order adds a term the order did not require and cannot itself be explained by it. > **Qualification / link.** The tradition does not settle on one interpretation of the silence, and the logical-semantic reading is a reconstruction rather than an explicit early theory, so a careful answer combines the therapeutic and presuppositional readings while acknowledging that the agnostic reading exists and is weaker.

prop-9828f44b2e8855509f35.normalized_semantic_payload: > **Claim.** The five standing objections to Buddhism are one objection about ownership, and recognising this converts a memorised list of criticisms into a single reusable analytical move. > **Named evidence.** The Nyāya line of Vātsyāyana, Uddyotakara and Udayana argues from recognition (*pratyabhijñā*), memory and moral desert; Kumārila Bhaṭṭa argues that word-meaning and duty require a self and real universals; Śaṃkara-type Advaita argues that liberation and the unity of the knower are unintelligible without a witness; and the realist nihilism charge argues that emptiness leaves nothing for ethics or knowledge. > **Analysis.** Each objection takes a function that Buddhism retains — remembering, meaning, being liberated, acting well — and argues that the function requires a bearer Buddhism has removed.
